London, 13<sup>th</sup> March 2009 



# Norilsk Nickel Daily News Digest 

**Anooraq Resources’** financing strategy to buy certain South African platinum assets from Anglo Platinum were at an advanced stage, the company said yesterday.  Anooraq and its biggest shareholder, Pelawan Investments, are in talks on a financing strategy for the acquisition of 51% of the Lebowa platinum mine and an additional 1% controlling interest in each of the Ga-Phasha, Boikgantsho and Kwanda JV projects. A  joint technical review of the current Anglo Platinum-approved mine plan and capital program for Lebowa, is currently being finalised, and an updated technical report on Lebowa is being prepared. _Source:  Mining Weekly_ 

**South Africa’s total mining production** for January was down 11%, compared with January 2008, owing to negative contributions from the platinum-group metals (PGMs), diamond and chromium sectors. Official data released by Statistics South Africa showed that PGMs had contributed 2,3% to the decline. The total mining production for the three months ended January 2009, after seasonal adjustment, had decreased by 10,7%, compared with the prior quarter. PGMs had contributed 5,7% of this. _Source:  Mining Weekly_ 

**Platfields** will list on the main board of the JSE “within weeks” and raise capital on the exchange in July. Platfields CEO Bongani Mbindwane said that the company had chosen July as a target date for the raising of the first tranche of R200-million to coincide the 50% tax break for mining juniors, which was gazetted last week.  Platfields intended remaining independent. The current focus was to drill the company’s four properties in order to prove up the resources and the reserves and then to mine them.  The company was targeting millions of ounces of platinum-group elements (PGEs) across all three of its PGE properties.  Its principal Berg project was close to Anglo Platinum’s Der Brochen project and Aquarius’ Everest South. _Source:  Mining Weekly_ 

**General Motors** has told the federal task force on the automotive industry that it will not need $2 billion in loans this month.  It still, however, thinks it will need the full $22.5 billion in loans this year that it requested in a viability report last month.  “We still could need to get up to $18 billion in loans in April, but we’re reviewing that now with the Treasury,” said a GM spokesman.  GM has been negotiating with the UAW to gain concessions to help the company get more government funding. A source familiar with those talks says GM did “far better” than Ford in terms of the contract givebacks.  But GM has not made much progress on negotiating stock as payment for half of its $20 billion funding obligation for the UAW Voluntary Employees’ Beneficiary Association retiree health care fund. _Source:  Automotive News_ 

**European car sales plunged** 18% in February as the global recession stifled demand for Opel, Mercedes-Benz and BMW models, especially in the once- booming

eastern part of the continent. Registrations fell to 968,159 vehicles last month from 1.19 million a year earlier, the European Automobile Manufacturers’ Association said today. It was the sharpest February drop since the organization began recording data in 1990 and follows a 27% drop in January, which was the steepest in a contraction that has extended to 10 months.  Volkswagen AG predicted a first-quarter loss yesterday. BMW said 2008 net income plunged 89% after it took charges for bad loans and leases.  Industry deliveries in eastern Europe fell 30% to 66,123 vehicles; Romania dropped 67%, and Hungary declined 46%. Poland, the region’s largest market, bucked the trend, posting an increase of 7.3% to 30,194 cars and sport-utility vehicles. In western Europe, demand fell 17% to 902,037 vehicles, as the Spanish market plunged 49% and the U.K. dropped 22%. Auto sales collapsed in Iceland, where the economy capsized after the island nation’s biggest banks failed to refinance their debt. 91 new vehicles registered in the country in February compared with 1,035 a year earlier. 

_Source:  Bloomberg_
